lines.en: It is impossible to remove all risk from life; the best we can do is to manage it wisely.
What the accident taught the company was that safety rules are written in the blood of past mistakes.
Not until the bridge collapsed did the authorities take the warnings seriously.
However careful a driver you are, the road always carries risks you cannot control.
The device is designed to shut down automatically, were the temperature to rise beyond the safe limit.
It is often the risks we ignore, not the ones we fear, that end up hurting us.
Little did the passengers know that a simple check had prevented a disaster that morning.
Were everyone to follow the safety instructions, most accidents would never happen.
What matters is not whether accidents can happen, but whether we are prepared when they do.
Rarely does fear protect us as well as preparation does.
What investigations usually reveal is not one big error, but a chain of small ignored warnings.
It is human nature to believe that accidents happen to other people, never to us.
Only after the fire did the building's owners install the alarms they had been advised to fit years earlier.
Were the workers to report every near miss, the company could prevent most serious accidents.
However advanced the warning system may be, it is worthless if nobody reacts to it.
